page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU derived from a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processor, with one physical core and one thread per core. The instance provides 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, allocating a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local instance storage is not included, requiring external EBS volumes, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps with no bundled public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance alongside predictable constraints tied to its single-thread layout. In the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core suite, the AMD processor scores in the top 25%, registering 3031.18 and 1943.0 points respectively. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which aid vector operations and lightweight machine learning inference, where it achieves 107.26 tokens per second on small 135M model generation. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics, software compilation, and overall database throughput fall into the bottom 10% to 25% due to the limitation of having only one physical execution thread.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the c7a.medium provides dedicated compute capacity without the burstable credit throttling typical of entry-level general-purpose machines. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and limited baseline network capability require careful architectural planning for input-output heavy applications. The instance is suited for lightweight single-threaded microservices, background job workers, small-scale batch utilities, and low-concurrency web components that require modern CPU instructions on a lean memory footprint.
